text:
maria (platform): heads-up — saw a spike on eu-west yesterday where customers on Pro started getting 429s for the new llama-70b-primary. We should consider capacity-based model-variant failover rather than region fallback.

todd (eng-runtime): +1. region fallback increases latency. idea: if primary model is saturated, route to pre-configured variant (quantized / smaller) that is latency-compatible.

sasha (eng-platform): clarifying Qs — precedence: tier -> region -> model-variant? If we do model-variant first, enterprise customers might expect dedicated capacity to be honored.

lee (ml-infra): suggestion: policy order should be: dedicated-reserve (if reserved capacity exists) -> model-variant fallback -> region fallback -> queued. That keeps SLAs for Dedicated.

anya (product): product note: console UX needs to show when fallback happens and which variant served — customers will want attribution for billing and quality regressions. Add trace IDs.

maria (platform): agreed. telemetry must include: original_model, served_model, reason (capacity), latency, tokens, fallback_count. Also need alerting when fallback rate > 5% for > 5m.

todd (eng-runtime): prototyping a small API change: add optional route_policy on request and a server-side policy that can be pushed via config. Example config:

```
route_policy:
  - reserved_capacity: true
  - model_variant_fallback:
      order: [quant8, quant4, cpu-optimized]
      threshold_qps: 0.85
  - region_fallback: true
```

sasha (eng-platform): watch out — we need compatibility checks (tokenizer, function-calling support). Can't silently fallback to variant that doesn't support tools.

lee (ml-infra): we'll add capability flags to model registry and runtime will validate before routing. Fallback should only pick compatible variants.

anya (product): UX: show on rollout card a toggle "Enable model-variant failover" with two modes: soft (telemetry only) and active. Soft mode emits events but doesn't change routing.

maria (platform): sounds good. acceptance criteria:
- runtime implements model-variant fallback respecting reserved capacity
- console exposes failover toggle and per-route metrics
- telemetry fields emitted and visible in trace/event logs
- canary rollout: start soft for 24h, then enable active for smaller customer subset

todd (eng-runtime): I'll spike a canary PR today. plan: soft=true by default, no billing changes until product confirms. cc @sasha for API review.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for eng-runtime/spikes/model-fallback-spike

infra-alerts: observed: eu-west llama-70b-primary saturated at 2026-02-08T14:12:03Z (RPS 1.2x expected capacity)

sasha (eng-platform): TY. I'll draft the API changelog and an internal runbook for support (how to surface fallback incidents to customers).
